quest.title: Valor's Afterglow: The Faint Light Remembered
quest.description: Zhiqiong seems to have left the exploration team to explore on her own. Still, it's too dangerous to go alone into The Chasm, so she must be found...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Primogem x20, Mora x10000

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yikes! Y—You scared me!

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: S—Sorry. Anyway, um, if you're looking for Zhiqiong... she left.

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: I don't know... I was distracted for just a few moments, and that was it — she was gone.

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: I had a talk with her... but she insisted on leaving. I doubt I could have cajoled or browbeat her, or even beat her into staying.

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: *sigh* I just hope she knows what she's doing.

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: I really do hope so...

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: Ugh, right, I have to tell Muning, and get him to organize a search party for that kid!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, that Zhiqiong, she's gone again! Let's get back to the surface and look for Muning, quickly!

choices.text: How was she doing when she left?

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: Khedive did a check-up, and he said that it didn't look too promising...

talks.objective: Talk to Muning about Zhiqiong's departure

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Hmm? Zhiqiong's not with you? Word's come down from the Ministry.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: On account of the invaluable help that her maps have brought to the Huishan Hall, the Ministry of Civil Affairs has decided to make an exception for her and... Let me see, invite her to be formally accepted as a consultant and guide.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Congratulations to her are in order — it seems that all that running around wasn't for naught.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Left? What do you mean? Do you mean she left first? But the Millelith didn't tell me of anyone leaving The Chasm...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Hang on a moment, you mean she left the exploration team?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: As in, Zhiqiong left the team?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes! Which part of that didn't you get?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: ...I get it. I will put a search and rescue party together immediately. If she is still in The Chasm, we should be able to find her.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: She might just be doing something harebrained again, or perhaps she left for another reason... But regardless, we must find her.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: In her current condition, working away from the team is simply far too reckless...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: No, I don't reckon so... I suppose it's about time I stepped in as well.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll be there if you need me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon too! We can't just leave our junior adventurer behind!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll look out while on the road as well. Who knows, maybe we'll bump into her somehow!

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: She's a restless one, but whatever the case, we are still friends. I might not be the friendliest person around, but I don't simply forget friendships just like that.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: She's always talking about some big adventurer's dream or something, and she's actually been injured quite seriously several times before. Nearly bit it on at least one occasion, too. And here I thought she'd settled down for a bit...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: I'd hoped that she'd have forgotten those unrealistic dreams of hers already. Roald... Stanley... It's not all wine and roses with them, you know!

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: *sigh* But I never expected... To be honest, I was starting to wonder if asking you to come to The Chasm was the right decision... If we hadn't, she might not have had a fire lit under her again...

choices.text: Her efforts did produce some results in the end.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Results...? I think that's a bit too utilitarian. We are very grateful for the maps that she drew of large swathes of The Chasm, yes...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: But should intangible, illusory things like "dreams" and pursuing them really come before one's life?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: I just can't understand it, nor can I imagine anyone really plunging into danger over things like that.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: As such, please leave the search for her to me... Uh, more accurately, just leave it to the Millelith search party.

choices.text: It is her choice, you know.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Choice, you say... Excuses! She's going there to die, don't you realize that!?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: ...*cough* Sorry, I spoke a little harshly there. Still... couldn't she just exercise a little more patience in the face of things that we mortals cannot change!?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: In twenty or thirty years... maybe even ten, we might have safer underground equipment! Then, she wouldn't have to worry about having to go on expeditions to make underground maps.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: But she's not willing to wait for any of these things, not at all! No, she just has to finish an entire life's work while she's still so young!

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: It's folly, I say, and as a friend, I can't just leave her be.
